texts.li: It's the shortest night of the year, and {A_nameDef} wants a bonfire, a proper one taller than the roof, with singing and drinking and the night shift let off for once.\n\nIt would burn through a good stack of firewood.
{A_nameDef} has spent a week stacking logs behind the barn for midsummer, and has finally asked the council for permission to light them.

li.label: Light the bonfire
li.outcome: The midsummer fire burned until dawn, and most of the colony was still around it when the sun came up.

li.label: Save the wood this year
li.outcome: No bonfire. {A_nameDef} sat on the log pile all evening, looking at it.

li.label: A small fire, no drinking
li.outcome: They had a small fire and went to bed early. {A_nameDef} called it "a candle with ambitions."

texts.li: The last of the crops are in. {A_nameDef}, who planted most of them, wants a harvest supper with second helpings for everyone. It would cost about {COUNT} raw food.\n\nThe stores will have to last the winter either way.

{A_nameDef} has spent the whole season in the fields and is asking for one night to celebrate, a harvest home costing about {COUNT} raw food. "We grew it," {A_nameDef} says. "We should get to taste it."

li.label: A harvest feast for everyone
li.outcome: The harvest home went on late, and even the cook had seconds.

li.label: Store every scrap for winter
li.outcome: Every grain went into storage for the winter. {A_nameDef} thinks a season's work deserved better.

li.label: A modest supper
li.outcome: They had a good meal, nothing extravagant, and the stores hardly felt it.

texts.li: It's the longest night of the year, dark by mid-afternoon and bitterly cold. {A_nameDef} thinks the colony should mark it the way people did back home, with extra food and a long evening around the fire.
Last night {A_nameDef} found the colonists huddled in separate rooms, each alone with the cold. "It's midwinter," {A_nameDef} told the council. "We should be together for it."

li.label: Extra rations for the long night
li.outcome: The colony ate well on the longest night, and there was singing afterward.

li.label: Stories by the fire, no feast
li.outcome: They spent the evening telling stories around the fire, some sad, some filthy, until the fire burned down.

li.label: Just another night
li.outcome: The longest night passed like any other, cold and dark and quiet.

ColonyCouncil.DilemmaDef.label: naming the year

texts.li: It started as a joke at dinner, the idea that the new year needs a name, and now the colony is arguing about it. {A_nameDef} has proposed "the year of {A_nameDef}," loudly and often.\n\nThe council has been asked to settle it.

Someone decided the annals need a name for the new year. {A_nameDef} has put forward {A_possessive} own name, with a straight face. Others want to name it for the colony's dead, and one person keeps suggesting the muffalo.

ColonyCouncil.DilemmaDef.traditionLabel: naming the year after a muffalo

li.label: The year of {A_nameDef}
li.outcome: This is now officially the year of {A_nameDef}. {A_nameDef} has mentioned it a dozen times since breakfast.

li.label: Name it for those we lost
li.outcome: The year carries the names of the dead, and the arguing stopped.

li.label: The year of the muffalo
li.outcome: It is the year of the muffalo. The muffalo has not been told. {A_nameDef} is sulking.

texts.li: The raiders left plenty behind: boots, coats, a weapon or two still in good shape. {A_nameDef} did most of the shooting and thinks that earns {A_objective} first pick.\n\nSome of the others disagree.
The bodies are still warm, and the argument over their gear has already started. {A_nameDef}, who killed three of them, has claimed the best of it.

li.label: {A_nameDef} earned first pick
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} took the best of the spoils. A few of the others grumble that they fought too.

li.label: Share everything equally
li.outcome: The spoils went to the common stores, to be shared out equally. Most think that's fair. {A_nameDef} doesn't, and says so.

li.label: The fighters get the spoils
li.outcome: Everyone who fought got a share. Those who stayed inside got nothing but the cleanup, and some of them resent it.

li.label: Let the quartermaster share it out
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} sorted the spoils by need: coats to whoever was cold, boots to whoever's had worn through. {A_nameDef} got one good thing out of it and has stopped arguing.

outcomes.li: [lowtech] {B_nameDef} laid the spoils out on the threshing floor and handed them out one by one, by need. {A_nameDef} got the bow {A_pronoun} wanted and nothing else, and seems content with that.
[!lowtech] {B_nameDef} wrote every item down, then shared them out by need. {A_nameDef} got the rifle {A_pronoun} wanted and has stopped arguing.
[b:trait:Kind] {B_nameDef} gave the warmest coats to the ones who stood watch longest, and the rest by need. Even {A_nameDef} said it was fair.

li.riskOutcome: {B_nameDef} shared the spoils out by need, and {A_nameDef} ended up with a pair of boots two sizes too big. The argument has moved from the council to the quartermaster.

li.reason: Needs a quartermaster on the council

texts.li: The raiders lie where they fell. {A_nameDef} asks what the council wants done with them: graves, a pyre, or the treeline and the scavengers.\n\nThe colony is divided on it, and loudly.
{A_nameDef} has been standing over the bodies outside the wall since the fighting stopped. "They were people," {A_nameDef} says. "Somebody's people. What do we do with them?"

li.label: Give them graves
li.outcome: The raiders were buried outside the colony, which took most of a day. Some colonists slept better for it; others resent the work.

li.label: Burn them
li.outcome: The bodies were burned on a pyre that went all night. The smell hung over the colony until morning.

li.label: Drag them to the treeline
li.outcome: The bodies were dragged to the treeline. The scavengers came at dusk, and they could be heard from inside the walls.

li.label: One grave for all of them
li.outcome: The raiders went into one long trench outside the wall, filled in before dark. {A_nameDef} said a few words over it.

outcomes.li: [winter] The ground was too hard for more than one grave, so the raiders share a shallow one under the snow outside the wall. {A_nameDef} piled stones on top.
[trait:Kind] One trench for all of them, filled in before dark. {A_nameDef} wanted names on it and settled for a count.

texts.li: The colony has come through the attack, and everyone still standing is giddy with relief. {A_nameDef} wants to celebrate properly with a victory feast tonight, using about {COUNT} raw food.\n\nThe repairs would have to wait until morning.
The fighting stopped an hour ago, and {A_nameDef} is already asking the council for a feast. "We earned it," {A_nameDef} says, wiping someone else's blood off {A_possessive} sleeve.

li.label: A victory feast
li.outcome: They ate and drank until well after dark, loud with relief.

li.label: Repairs first, celebrations later
li.outcome: It was straight back to work on the walls, the wounded and the bodies. The celebration never happened.

li.label: A quick hot meal, then the walls
li.outcome: Everyone ate a hot meal standing up, and the repairs started before the bowls were cleared.

outcomes.li: [winter] A pot of something hot went round the yard, and they ate it with their gloves on before going back to the walls.
[colony:Hardworking] A hot meal and back to work, as usual here. {A_nameDef} ate {A_possessive} share slowly, to make it last.

li.label: Have the best cook stretch half the food
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} made a feast out of half the food anyone expected, mostly stew and nerve, and the colony ate until late.

outcomes.li: [lowtech] {B_nameDef} had three pots going over the fire at once and fed everyone twice from half the stores. The walls waited until morning.
[b:trait:Gourmand] {B_nameDef} cooked as if for a lord's table and ate as much as anyone, but the food lasted. It was a good night.

li.riskOutcome: {B_nameDef} tried to stretch the food too far, and the feast ran out before the second round. Everyone ate, at least.
